subject: Clarify default retention: what we keep and when it gets deleted (requests vs model outputs)
messages:
From: Elise Park <elise.park@orchidhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Orchid Health Legal <legal@orchidhealth.com>
Date: 2025-03-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Q on default retention for demo environment

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency/throughput looked promising. Before we move further I need a concise explanation for our InfoSec team: what does Redwood persist by default from an API call? Specifically:

- Do you store the exact request payload (user prompt) by default?
- Do you persist the model response (generated output) and for how long?
- What about intermediate/streamed fragments (partial tokens) and KV cache traces — are those retained?

We're most concerned about PHI/PII passing through prompts and whether we need to keep additional safeguards enabled.

If you have a one-page summary or a short matrix we can share with our legal folks, that would help.

Best,
Elise
Elise Park
Director of Integrations, Orchid Health

Attachment: Orchid_Retention_Questions.docx (docx)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elise Park <elise.park@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-03-07T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on default retention for demo environment

Hi Elise — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short answer below and attached a PDF summary for sharing with your InfoSec team. TL;DR: by default we retain request inputs and final model outputs for a short, configurable horizon; derivative artifacts are handled differently. Details: 

1) Request payloads (user prompts / API input): retained by default in hosted accounts for 45 days to support debugging, billing, and abuse detection. Customers on Dedicated/Private can opt out or set a shorter horizon (including immediate non-persistence) via account settings or contract.

2) Final model responses (completed outputs): retained by default for 45 days as well; used for quality monitoring, billing reconciliation, and safety review. If you enable the "no-retain" flag at request time or have an enterprise contract option, we treat outputs as ephemeral and do not persist final responses.

3) Streamed fragments (partial tokens): short-lived in-memory buffers used to assemble streaming responses. For hosted customers, fragments are not written to long-term storage by default unless the request completes and the final output is persisted. There are narrow diagnostics modes that may persist streamed fragments for a limited time with explicit consent.

4) KV cache / runtime traces: KV cache entries are ephemeral and kept only for the lifetime of the model session; they are not stored to customer-visible logs unless you use a debug dump feature. Runtime traces (e.g., internal logs, tokenization traces) are captured for telemetry and rotated per retention policies; sensitive fields are redacted where possible.

5) Attachments / file uploads: if your prompt includes file attachments processed by Redwood (e.g., embeddings), those are stored in object storage and follow the same default 45-day horizon unless you configure a different lifecycle or request deletion.

6) Deletion and evidence: we provide erasure APIs and proof-of-deletion artifacts for data covered by our retention policies. For Hosted customers, deletion may take up to 72 hours to propagate to backups; Dedicated/Private customers get contractually tighter windows.

I've attached a concise matrix and a short FAQ for the common follow-ons. If Orchid needs a sub-45-day default or a contractual no-retain option we can loop Legal/Contracts; Kimberly and Ben are looped here to support that discussion.

Next step: would you like a short call with our Security team to walk your InfoSec through the matrix and the erasure evidence flow?

Cheers,
Sean
Sean Gallagher

Looping Legal in if Orchid asks for contract changes. A couple of clarifications to Sean's note we should make explicit in the matrix for their InfoSec: 

- Default horizon (45 days) applies to both requests and final outputs in Hosted unless the tenancy-level flag is flipped.
- Streaming fragments are not durable unless you intentionally enable diagnostics; emphasize that streamed tokens do not make it into persistent logs by default.
- Provide a short bullet on EU data residency: for EU region-hosted accounts the residency of persisted logs follows the region and secondary backups may be geo-located per config. 

I'll draft a one-paragraph legal-friendly blurb and Ben can take the lead on any SOW changes.

Hi Sean / Kim,

Thanks for the summary. A couple of follow-ups from our InfoSec review: 

1) Can you confirm whether model debugging traces ever include raw prompt contents in backups or logs outside the 45-day window? We need assurance that once deletion is requested, we can get evidence that prompts were removed from backups.

2) If a hospital-level PHI-containing prompt is submitted by a user, what immediate measures do you recommend (aside from contract-level no-retain) to ensure the prompt isn't preserved? Are there request-time headers we can set to enforce non-persistence?

3) For the erasure API, what is the SLA for returning proof-of-deletion and what does the proof artifact look like?

We'd like to schedule a 30-minute call with your Security operations team next week. Please provide 2 windows.

Regards,
Orchid Health Legal

Hi — appreciate the detailed questions. Short answers below and then I'll have Security Ops join the call. Proposed slots: Tue 2025-03-11 09:00-09:30 PT or Wed 2025-03-12 14:00-14:30 PT. 

Answers: 
1) Debug traces: we do not surface raw prompts into long-term backup archives as part of routine debug traces. If diagnostics are enabled and a dump is requested, that dump is stored in a secure object store and follows the same retention lifecycle; however, our standard backup snapshots (used for infra resilience) are encrypted and retention/restore operations are subject to a 72-hour deletion propagation window. We can provide a deletion certificate showing the keys were rotated and objects removed per request.

2) For PHI: request-time "no-retain" header (x-redwood-no-retain: true) will instruct the runtime to avoid persisting requests or outputs. For Hosted customers without an explicit contract, we also offer a token-level filter that identifies likely PHI and redacts or routes to a secure processing path. Recommend using the no-retain header plus an allowlist of endpoints for high-sensitivity traffic.

3) Erasure API SLA: standard is 72 hours to provide proof-of-deletion for Hosted accounts; Dedicated/Private can be contractually reduced to 24 hours. The proof-of-deletion artifact includes a keyed hash of the removed objects, timestamp, and the deletion operation ID linked to an audit record in our console.

Action items: Kim will prepare the legal blurb and Ben will scope SOW options for a no-retain contract addendum. Security Ops (cc'd on the upcoming invite) will present the deletion evidence format on the call.

Thanks — let me know which slot works and we'll send a calendar invite with the Security Ops attendees.

Sean

Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
